people.name: David Sassoon
people.note: Of the family that arrived in Bombay in 1832. Built institutions in the city that still serve Indian society.

people.name: Lieutenant General J. F. R. Jacob
people.note: Recognised for his contribution during the 1971 war with Pakistan.

people.name: Walter Kaufmann
people.note: Composed the signature tune for All India Radio.

people.name: Doctor Reuben David
people.note: Founder of the Kankaria Zoo in Ahmedabad.

people.name: David Abraham Cheulkar
people.note: An actor who became a household name across the country.

people.name: Edwyn Myers
people.note: Gave shape to the Films Division of India.

people.name: The Jam Saheb of Nawanagar
people.field: Refuge during the Second World War
people.note: Offered refuge to Polish children, including Jewish children, during the Holocaust.

people.name: Eliyau Bezalel
people.note: Recipient of the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman in 2005.

people.name: Sheikh Munir Ansari
people.note: Recipient of the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman in 2011.

people.name: Doctor Lael A. Best
people.note: Recipient of the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman in 2017.

people.name: Reena Vinod Pushkarna
people.note: Recipient of the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman in 2023.

people.name: Nissim Ezekiel
people.note: Britannica describes him as one of the founders of the English vernacular literary genre in India, and as the father of post-independence English-language verse in India. He is the single most consequential figure this section contains, and his community identity is almost never mentioned alongside his work.

people.name: Esther David
people.note: A Sahitya Akademi winner who has spent a working life writing the Bene Israel of Ahmedabad into Indian literature, and who trained as a sculptor and illustrates her own books.

people.name: Ruby Daniel
people.note: The first Cochin Jewish woman to author a book, and the person who translated roughly 120 Malayalam Jewish women's songs into English before they were lost.

people.name: Jael Silliman
people.field: Writer, academic, archivist, born, year not confirmed
people.note: Built the digital archive of Jewish Calcutta, which is the closest thing to a model for what this project is trying to do for the country as a whole.

people.name: Sheela Rohekar
people.field: Novelist in Hindi and Gujarati, born October 1942
people.note: Described by a scholar at Uppsala University as the single living Jewish author of fine literature writing in Hindi.

people.name: Zilka Joseph
people.field: Poet, born, year not recorded here
people.note: A Bene Israel poet whose most recent book is built around the malida ceremony, the Bene Israel rite associated with the Prophet Elijah.

people.name: Sophie Judah
people.note: Nineteen linked stories set in an invented Bene Israel town, written by someone whose own childhood was spent as the only Jewish family in a series of real ones.

people.name: Haeem Samuel Kehimkar
people.note: Wrote the first history of his own community, in English, in 1897. It was published forty years later in Tel Aviv, twenty-eight years after his death.

people.name: Samuel Fyzee-Rahamin
people.note: Born Bene Israel in Poona, trained under John Singer Sargent, became in 1925 the first Muslim artist represented in the Tate. One life crosses three religious identities and four cities.

people.name: Siona Benjamin
people.note: Paints blue-skinned figures, in gouache and gold leaf, drawing on Indian and Persian miniature painting, illuminated manuscripts, comic books and Sephardic icons at once.

people.name: Anish Kapoor
people.note: Included here for one precise reason, and described carefully because this is exactly the kind of entry that gets exaggerated.

people.name: Shimon Lev
people.field: Artist, photographer, curator, scholar of India, born 1962
people.note: An Israeli artist whose doctorate was on the mutual influence of Jewish and Indian cultures, and who has written a book on Gandhi and Hermann Kallenbach.

people.name: Ruby Myers, known as Sulochana
people.note: A telephone operator from a Baghdadi Jewish family in Poona who became the highest paid film star in India, then learned Hindustani in a year in order to survive the arrival of sound.

people.name: Esther Victoria Abraham, known as Pramila
people.field: Stunt actress, the first woman film producer in the Hindi industry, 1916 to 2006
people.note: Won the first Miss India title in 1947 at the age of thirty-one, acted in around thirty films, and produced sixteen more through her own company.

people.name: Florence Ezekiel, known as Nadira
people.note: Played the definitive screen vamp of Hindi cinema for three decades, and was among the first Indian actresses to own a Rolls-Royce.

people.name: David Abraham Cheulkar
people.note: Appeared in more than a hundred and ten films across four decades, billed simply as David, and became one of the most recognisable faces in Indian cinema.

people.name: Ezra Mir, born Edwyn Myers
people.note: Worked on over seven hundred documentaries, became Chief Producer of the Films Division in 1956, and founded the Indian Documentary Producers Association in the same year.

people.name: Rose Musleah, known as Miss Rose
people.note: Acted from 1922 to 1945. Of her known films, exactly one is known to survive.

people.name: Pearl Padamsee
people.note: A central figure in Mumbai English-language theatre for four decades, with a Punjabi Christian father and a Baghdadi Jewish mother.

people.name: Joseph David Penkar
people.note: Wrote the Parsi play behind Alam Ara, India's first talkie, released on 14 March 1931 and now lost.

people.name: Walter Kaufmann
people.note: A Jewish refugee from Nazi Europe who wrote the signature tune of All India Radio, taught Zubin Mehta, and ended as a professor of musicology in Indiana.

people.name: The Iraqi Jewish musicians of the Bombay studios
people.field: Instrumentalists and singers, early to mid twentieth century
people.note: Oud, qanun and mandolin players from Baghdad and Samarkand who played on Hindi film soundtracks, and one Arabic tune that became a Hindi film song.

people.name: The Malayalam songs of Cochin Jewish women
people.field: Oral tradition, tradition of uncertain age, translated 1982 to 1999
people.note: A body of Jewish women's songs in Malayalam, roughly a hundred and twenty of which were translated into English by one woman in her seventies and eighties.
